I've worked out the plan below and didn't edit any files.

# Plan: exact numeric comparison for `eq`/`ne`/`lt`/`le`/`gt`/`ge` and `where`

## 1. New helper in `common/hreflect/helpers.go`

Add `"cmp"` and `"math"` to the imports, then add the following code (for example after `IsFloat`):

```go
// CompareNumbers compares a and b exactly (no lossy conversions).
// It returns false if a or b is not an int, uint or float, or is NaN.
func CompareNumbers(a, b reflect.Value) (int, bool) {
	ak, bk := a.Kind(), b.Kind()
	if !IsNumber(ak) || !IsNumber(bk) {
		return 0, false
	}
	if IsFloat(ak) && math.IsNaN(a.Float()) || IsFloat(bk) && math.IsNaN(b.Float()) {
		return 0, false
	}
	switch {
	case IsFloat(ak) && IsFloat(bk):
		return cmp.Compare(a.Float(), b.Float()), true
	case IsFloat(ak):
		c, _ := CompareNumbers(b, a)
		return -c, true
	case IsFloat(bk):
		if IsInt(ak) {
			return compareIntFloat(a.Int(), b.Float()), true
		}
		return compareUintFloat(a.Uint(), b.Float()), true
	case IsInt(ak) && IsInt(bk):
		return cmp.Compare(a.Int(), b.Int()), true
	case IsUint(ak) && IsUint(bk):
		return cmp.Compare(a.Uint(), b.Uint()), true
	case IsInt(ak):
		return compareIntUint(a.Int(), b.Uint()), true
	default:
		return -compareIntUint(b.Int(), a.Uint()), true
	}
}

func compareIntUint(i int64, u uint64) int {
	if i < 0 {
		return -1
	}
	return cmp.Compare(uint64(i), u)
}

func compareIntFloat(i int64, f float64) int {
	switch {
	case f >= 1<<63:
		return -1
	case f < -(1 << 63):
		return 1
	}
	t := math.Trunc(f)
	if c := cmp.Compare(i, int64(t)); c != 0 {
		return c
	}
	return cmp.Compare(t, f)
}

func compareUintFloat(u uint64, f float64) int {
	switch {
	case f < 0:
		return 1
	case f >= 1<<64:
		return -1
	}
	t := math.Trunc(f)
	if c := cmp.Compare(u, uint64(t)); c != 0 {
		return c
	}
	return cmp.Compare(t, f)
}
```

`±Inf` is covered by the range checks. NaN returns `ok=false`, so callers fall back to their existing IEEE behaviour (NaN is never equal to anything).

## 2. `tpl/compare/compare.go`

**`Namespace.Eq`:**
- Remove the `Int…`, `Float…` and `Uint…` cases from the `normalize` closure. Keep the nil, `AsTimeProvider`, `String` and default cases.
- Before the loop, add `fv := reflect.ValueOf(first)`.
- In the loop, after the two `compare.Eqer` checks and before `other = normalize(other)`, insert:
  ```go
  if c, ok := hreflect.CompareNumbers(fv, reflect.ValueOf(other)); ok {
  	if c == 0 {
  		return true
  	}
  	continue
  }
  ```

**`compareGetWithCollator`:**
- After the "Fast path: both values are plain strings" block, insert:
  ```go
  if c, ok := hreflect.CompareNumbers(reflect.ValueOf(a), reflect.ValueOf(b)); ok {
  	return float64(c), 0
  }
  ```
- In both `switch av.Kind()` and `switch bv.Kind()`:
  - Change the `Int…` case to just `left = float64(av.Int())` (and `right = float64(bv.Int())`), dropping the `IsUint` branch.
  - Merge `reflect.Uint64` into the `Uint…` case: `reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, reflect.Uint16, reflect.Uint32, reflect.Uint64:` → `left = float64(av.Uint())` (and the same for `right`). These cases still matter for number vs. string/bool/time pairs.
- Delete the `compareTwoUints` method; nothing else uses it.

`math` stays imported because it is still used by `IsInf` and `IsNaN`.

## 3. `tpl/collections/where.go` – `checkCondition`

Directly after the `tryEq` `switch op { ... }` block, and before `var ivp, imvp *int64`, insert:

```go
if c, ok := hreflect.CompareNumbers(v, mv); ok {
	switch op {
	case "", "=", "==", "eq":
		return c == 0, nil
	case "!=", "<>", "ne":
		return c != 0, nil
	case ">=", "ge":
		return c >= 0, nil
	case ">", "gt":
		return c > 0, nil
	case "<=", "le":
		return c <= 0, nil
	case "<", "lt":
		return c < 0, nil
	}
}
```

Also delete the same-kind `case reflect.Uint, reflect.Uint8, ..., reflect.Uint64:` branch. Its `int64(v.Uint())` cast overflows, and the new block above now covers it.

Leave the rest unchanged, including the mixed-number `ToFloat64E` branch. It still handles NaN and keeps the "no such operator" error for unknown ops.

**New `tpl/compare/compare_integration_test.go`** (package `compare_test`, with the license header)

```go
// TestCompareIntWithEqualFloat checks that eq/ne/lt/le/gt/ge agree for numerically equal int and float.
func TestCompareIntWithEqualFloat(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	files := `
-- hugo.toml --
disableKinds = ["page", "section", "taxonomy", "term", "rss", "sitemap"]
-- layouts/home.html --
eq: {{ eq 1 1.0 }}|ne: {{ ne 1 1.0 }}|lt: {{ lt 1 1.0 }}|le: {{ le 1 1.0 }}|gt: {{ gt 1 1.0 }}|ge: {{ ge 1 1.0 }}|
big: {{ eq 9007199254740993 9007199254740992.0 }}|{{ gt 9007199254740993 9007199254740992.0 }}|
`
	b := hugolib.Test(t, files)
	b.AssertFileContent("public/index.html",
		"eq: true|ne: false|lt: false|le: true|gt: false|ge: true|",
		"big: false|true|")
}
```

**`tpl/collections/collections_integration_test.go` → `TestWhereNumericIntFloat`**

```go
func TestWhereNumericIntFloat(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	files := `
-- hugo.toml --
disableKinds = ["taxonomy", "term", "rss", "sitemap"]
-- content/p1.md --
---
title: p1
n: 1
---
-- content/p2.md --
---
title: p2
n: 9007199254740993
---
-- layouts/page.html --
-- layouts/home.html --
eq1: {{ range where site.RegularPages "Params.n" "eq" 1.0 }}{{ .Title }}{{ end }}|
eqbig: {{ len (where site.RegularPages "Params.n" "eq" 9007199254740992.0) }}|
gtbig: {{ range where site.RegularPages "Params.n" "gt" 9007199254740992.0 }}{{ .Title }}{{ end }}|
`
	b := hugolib.Test(t, files)
	b.AssertFileContent("public/index.html", "eq1: p1|", "eqbig: 0|", "gtbig: p2|")
}
```

YAML integers decode as ints. If `n` arrives as a different int kind, the assertions still hold.

Also run `go test ./hugolib/... -run 'Sort|Where|Compare'`, because sorting (`collections.Sort`) uses `compare.Namespace` and its order for uint vs. negative int will change.

# Plan: exact numeric comparison shared by `eq`/`ne`/`lt`/`le`/`gt`/`ge` and `where`

## 1. New helper in `common/hreflect/helpers.go`

`hreflect` already imports `github.com/gohugoio/hugo/compare`, so the helper has to live in `hreflect`; putting it in `compare` would create an import cycle. Add `"cmp"` and `"math"` to the imports. Put this right after `IsFloat`:

```go
// CompareNumbers compares a and b exactly for any mix of int, uint and float kinds.
// ok is false if either is not a number or is NaN.
func CompareNumbers(a, b reflect.Value) (c int, ok bool) {
	ak, bk := a.Kind(), b.Kind()
	switch {
	case IsInt(ak):
		switch {
		case IsInt(bk):
			return cmp.Compare(a.Int(), b.Int()), true
		case IsUint(bk):
			return -compareUintInt(b.Uint(), a.Int()), true
		case IsFloat(bk):
			return compareIntFloat(a.Int(), b.Float())
		}
	case IsUint(ak):
		switch {
		case IsInt(bk):
			return compareUintInt(a.Uint(), b.Int()), true
		case IsUint(bk):
			return cmp.Compare(a.Uint(), b.Uint()), true
		case IsFloat(bk):
			return compareUintFloat(a.Uint(), b.Float())
		}
	case IsFloat(ak):
		switch {
		case IsInt(bk):
			c, ok := compareIntFloat(b.Int(), a.Float())
			return -c, ok
		case IsUint(bk):
			c, ok := compareUintFloat(b.Uint(), a.Float())
			return -c, ok
		case IsFloat(bk):
			af, bf := a.Float(), b.Float()
			if math.IsNaN(af) || math.IsNaN(bf) {
				return 0, false
			}
			return cmp.Compare(af, bf), true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

func compareUintInt(u uint64, i int64) int {
	if i < 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return cmp.Compare(u, uint64(i))
}

func compareIntFloat(i int64, f float64) (int, bool) {
	switch {
	case math.IsNaN(f):
		return 0, false
	case f >= 1<<63:
		return -1, true
	case f < -(1 << 63):
		return 1, true
	}
	t := math.Trunc(f)
	if c := cmp.Compare(i, int64(t)); c != 0 {
		return c, true
	}
	return cmp.Compare(t, f), true
}

func compareUintFloat(u uint64, f float64) (int, bool) {
	switch {
	case math.IsNaN(f):
		return 0, false
	case f < 0:
		return 1, true
	case f >= 1<<64:
		return -1, true
	}
	t := math.Trunc(f)
	if c := cmp.Compare(u, uint64(t)); c != 0 {
		return c, true
	}
	return cmp.Compare(t, f), true
}
```
